title: KV stride sensitivity simulator and safe-config apply orchestrator
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Goal: build a lightweight simulator and an orchestrated safe-apply workflow that lets operators explore cost vs quality trade-offs for KV/prefix caching changes, then apply TTL/policy/keying updates with automated safety checks and an auditable rollback path. The simulator uses a stride-based hit-sensitivity model (sequence-stride bucketing + stochastic sampling) to predict how changes to TTL, prefix merging, and cache key shaping affect hit-rate, downstream token costs, and tail latency. The orchestrator wires simulator outputs into a staged rollout: shadow replay -> micro-canary -> progressive pulse ramps -> auto-rollback. This ticket covers the simulator prototype, calibration with historical telemetry, integration points for the rollout orchestrator, and an operator runbook for manual override and incident response.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator produces hit-rate and token-cost forecasts for synthetic and at least two historical workloads with median error <= 7% and 90th percentile error <= 12% on validation runs
Rollout orchestrator supports a 4-phase apply: shadow replay, 0.5% micro-canary, 10% pulse ramp, 100% ramp, each with configurable safety gates
Automated rollback triggers defined and implemented: top-100 prefixes hit-rate drop >25% OR aggregate token-cost increase >15% OR 99th tail-latency regression >30%
Dashboard shows top N affected prefixes, predicted vs observed hit-rate deltas, and cost delta estimate for the active rollout
End-to-end tests for simulator calibration and orchestrator gating included in CI with synthetic telemetry fixtures
steps: Design stride-based hit-sensitivity model: define stride buckets, feature set (prefix popularity, sequence length distribution, request origin) and stochastic sampler
Implement simulator engine in Python with a small Rust performance-critical library for large prefix samplings
Calibrate model using 30 days of telemetry (prefix-level hits/misses, token counts, latency percentiles). Produce a calibration report
Add a safety policy module: compute rollback thresholds and sanity checks derived from simulator confidence intervals
Implement rollout orchestrator hooks: shadow-replay service, phased traffic-splitper, metric listener that enforces safety gates and can issue programmatic rollback
Build a simple UI panel in Console to preview simulator outputs and start a staged apply with defaults
Create operator runbook and alert rules; include CLI for emergency revert and for running simulator ad-hoc on a chosen prefix set
Ship PRs, run integration canary in staging, iterate based on results, then schedule prod pilot on non-critical tenant cohort
progress_updates: 2026-03-10 - Liam O'Connor: Kickoff. Documented model design and metrics matrix. Chose stride bucketing over fixed prefix grouping to better capture sequence-boundary effects. (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COST/ENG-764203-stride-model)

2026-03-11 - Priya Desai: Implemented initial sampler prototype and validated on 7-day telemetry subset. Early results show simulator overestimates hit uplift when naive prefix-merge is applied — need to add collision penalty term to model.

2026-03-12 - Priya Desai: Decided rollout phases and rollback thresholds in sync with SRE. Trade-off: tighter rollback thresholds reduce cost wins but significantly lower risk. Documented thresholds in runbook and added planned UI fields for operators to override with justification.
2026-03-12 - Liam O'Connor: Opened draft PR for simulator core and CI fixtures (GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1287). Next: add calibration job and safety policy module.
comments: Samira Patel (SRE): Please ensure the orchestrator exposes a dry-run mode that does not alter live routing and includes flame-graph traces for any increase in CPU per-request. We need to catch regressions that are orthogonal to cache hit-rate.

Ethan Zhou (PM): Request that the console preview displays both a conservative and aggressive cost forecast with confidence bands so product owners can choose risk profile. Also include a toggled explanation of key drivers (prefix merges, TTL increase, key canonicalization).
Design review (Mar 11): Small UI mockup approved; UX asked for an inline justification field required for manual override beyond default thresholds.
Action item: add a short acceptance test that simulates a suffix collision to verify the collision penalty reduces optimistic hit predictions. Assigned to Priya.
